newsitem.title: CHINA: Patten's autograph in Hong Kong now pricey trophy.
newsitem.headline: Patten's autograph in Hong Kong now pricey trophy.

text.p: Autographs of Hong Kong's last colonial governor Chris Patten have become valuable collectors' items in the two weeks since the territory's handover to China.
An auctioneer valued a Patten autograph signed before the July 1 sovereignty change at HK$17,900 (US$2,309), the South China Morning Post newspaper said on Friday.

"This figure is almost an Abraham Lincoln. It gets you two John F. Kennedys. It will get you Marilyn Monroe, Ernest Hemingway or a Sigmund Freud," said Bill Miller of the U.S. magazine Autograph Collector.

Patten signed hundreds of autographs for people before he left the territory. "The signature of Chris Patten on the day of the handover would be far greater than his signature as a politician in England," said expert Julian Brown.
But he compared Patten's signature to short-lived crazes such as the Cabbage Patch Doll, and added: "I wouldn't put much money on it appreciating."
